summary.text: A 66-year-old woman with a 30-pack-year smoking history presented with hemoptysis; chest CT showed a right lower lobe mass with obstructive pneumonia and N2 nodes (stage IIIB, T3N2M0), and staging studies ruled out systemic metastasis.
Serum CEA, ProGRP and NSE were elevated; biopsy confirmed small cell carcinoma, and genomic profiling showed FBXW7, KRAS, PTEN and RB1 alterations with TMB 17.65 muts/Mb.

She received three cycles of neoadjuvant etoposide, carboplatin and serplulimab with biomarker normalization and partial response at 2 months, then, after multidisciplinary consultation and her preference for surgery, underwent VATS right lower lobectomy.

Pathology showed no residual carcinoma in the primary site or lymph nodes (pathological complete response); postoperative analysis showed only PTEN mutation at 1.50%, undetectable TMB and negative PD-L1.

summary.text: A 70-year-old man with a 40-pack-year smoking history presented with cough and white sputum; chest CT showed a lobulated right lower lobe mass with pleural thickening and enlarged mediastinal nodes (stage IIIB, T4N2M0) and staging studies ruled out systemic metastasis.
Biopsy confirmed poorly differentiated small cell carcinoma, and genomic analysis showed MET fusion, PTEN, TP53 and MYC alterations with TMB 23.72 muts/Mb.

He received three cycles of neoadjuvant etoposide, carboplatin and serplulimab with partial response after cycle 2 and progression after cycle 3, was assessed as stable disease by the multidisciplinary team, and chose surgery.

VATS lobectomy showed residual poorly differentiated carcinoma with vascular invasion; post-treatment profiling showed changed MET, PTEN, MYC and TMB values and PD-L1 TPS 20%, CPS 30%; the source gives conflicting outcome statements.
